instructions.name: accept_offer
docs: Take a funded offer. Signed by whoever currently holds the authorities.
One instruction: every authority moves to the buyer and the money moves to the
seller. Because the seller signs this themselves, the program never needs custody
of the token — and the token program rejects the whole thing if the signer is not
really the authority, so no separate ownership check is needed or trusted.

accounts.name: seller
docs: Whoever currently holds the authorities. Verified by the token program itself.

accounts.name: reward_pool
docs: Supplied whenever the deal owes stakers a share. Its address is the program's
own PDA, so a caller cannot substitute a pool they control.

instructions.name: buy_token
docs: Buy a token listing. Pays the seller and the treasury, and transfers every
escrowed authority to the buyer, in a single instruction. There is no window in
which one side has both the money and the asset.

accounts.name: reward_pool
docs: Supplied whenever the deal owes stakers a share. Its address is the program's
own PDA, so a caller cannot substitute a pool they control.

instructions.name: cancel
docs: Seller withdraws an unsold listing. Any escrowed authorities go back to them.

instructions.name: cancel_offer
docs: Withdraw an offer and take the money back. The buyer may do this at any time;
anyone may do it once the offer has expired, so stale bids cannot linger.

accounts.name: signer
docs: The buyer, or after expiry anybody at all.

instructions.name: claim
docs: Withdraw earned SOL. Pays out of `owed` only, so the pool's own rent is never
touched and the account cannot be drained closed.

instructions.name: close_listing
docs: Reclaim the rent from a finished listing. Only the seller, only once terminal.

instructions.name: create_listing
docs: Open a listing. Token listings start as `Draft` and only become purchasable once
every promised authority is in the program's custody.

accounts.name: mint
docs: Required for token and pump listings, absent for off-chain ones.

instructions.name: dispute
docs: Freeze a funded deal pending arbitration. Either party may call it.

instructions.name: escrow_authority
docs: Seller hands one authority to the program. Once all promised authorities are in,
the listing goes live. This is what makes a token sale safe for the buyer: the
seller gives up control before anyone can pay.

instructions.name: fund
docs: Escrow the buyer's money for a deal whose asset cannot live on this program.
Starts the delivery clock.

instructions.name: init_reward_pool
docs: Open the reward pool. One per program, fixed to a single mint.
Deliberately separate from `initialize`: the marketplace works with no pool at
all, which is what lets it run before the coin exists.

accounts.name: vault
docs: Holds the staked tokens. Owned by the pool PDA, so only the program can move them.

instructions.name: initialize
docs: One-time setup of the fee, treasury and arbitrator.

instructions.name: make_offer
docs: Bid on a token nobody has listed.
The buyer's SOL locks in this account. It is a real, checkable commitment rather
than a message: anyone reading the chain can see the money is there.

instructions.name: refund
docs: Return the escrowed money to the buyer. Callable by ANYONE once the deadline has
passed, so a buyer whose seller vanished never needs the operator's cooperation.

accounts.name: signer
docs: Whoever is invoking. `refund` accepts anyone, the others check this key.

accounts.name: reward_pool
docs: Supplied whenever the deal owes stakers a share. Its address is the program's
own PDA, so a caller cannot substitute a pool they control.

instructions.name: release
docs: Buyer confirms delivery. Pays the seller and the treasury out of escrow.

accounts.name: signer
docs: Whoever is invoking. `refund` accepts anyone, the others check this key.

accounts.name: reward_pool
docs: Supplied whenever the deal owes stakers a share. Its address is the program's
own PDA, so a caller cannot substitute a pool they control.

instructions.name: resolve
docs: The arbitrator's only power: on a disputed deal, choose who wins. It cannot send
the money anywhere other than the seller or the buyer.

accounts.name: signer
docs: Whoever is invoking. `refund` accepts anyone, the others check this key.

accounts.name: reward_pool
docs: Supplied whenever the deal owes stakers a share. Its address is the program's
own PDA, so a caller cannot substitute a pool they control.

instructions.name: stake
docs: Put tokens in and start earning from the next sale onward.

accounts.name: from
docs: The staker's own token account. Must be for the pool's mint.

instructions.name: unstake
docs: Take tokens back out. Anything already earned stays owed and is still claimable,
so leaving never costs a staker rewards they had accrued.

accounts.name: from
docs: The staker's own token account. Must be for the pool's mint.

instructions.name: update_config
docs: Rotate the arbitrator, treasury or default fee. Never touches listing funds, and
listings already created keep the fee they were created with.

fields.name: authority
docs: May rotate the arbitrator, treasury and default fee. Cannot touch listing funds.

fields.name: arbitrator
docs: May only choose a winner on a disputed listing. Cannot redirect funds.

fields.name: treasury
docs: Receives the platform fee.

fields.name: fee_bps
docs: Default fee for new listings, in basis points.

fields.name: rewards_bps
docs: How much of `fee_bps` belongs to stakers rather than to the treasury.
300 of 500 means three of the five points go to holders.
Deliberately the last field: accounts written before this existed read it back as
zero, which means "no holder share" — the safe reading, and it lets the upgrade
land without migrating anything.

fields.name: buyer
docs: Set when funded or bought. Default until then.

fields.name: mint
docs: The SPL mint for token and pump listings. Default for off-chain listings.

fields.name: listing_id
docs: Client-chosen id, part of this account's address.

fields.name: fee_bps
docs: Frozen at creation, so a fee change can never be applied to a live deal.

fields.name: escrowed_lamports
docs: Lamports of buyer money this account is currently holding, excluding rent.

fields.name: deadline
docs: Unix timestamp after which `refund` becomes callable by anyone.

fields.name: authorities
docs: Authorities this listing promises.

fields.name: escrowed
docs: Authorities actually in the program's custody.

fields.name: rewards_bps
docs: Frozen at creation alongside `fee_bps`, so changing the split can never be
applied to a deal that is already live. Zero on listings that predate it.

types.name: Offer
docs: An unsolicited, funded bid on a token nobody has listed.
The mirror image of a `Listing`: instead of the seller escrowing the asset and
waiting for money, the buyer escrows the money and waits for the asset. Whoever
actually holds the authorities can accept, and because they sign that transaction
themselves the authorities move straight to the buyer — this account never needs
custody of them.
The owner does not need an account here, or to have heard of this marketplace.

fields.name: offer_id
docs: Client-chosen id, part of this account's address.

fields.name: fee_bps
docs: Frozen when the offer is made, so a fee change cannot be applied to a live bid.

fields.name: escrowed_lamports
docs: Lamports of the buyer's money this account holds, excluding rent.

fields.name: expiry
docs: Unix timestamp after which anyone may clean this up and return the money.

fields.name: authorities
docs: Which authorities the buyer is bidding for.

fields.name: rewards_bps
docs: Frozen when the offer is made, for the same reason `fee_bps` is.

types.name: RewardPool
docs: Where the holders' share of every fee accumulates.
Solana has no way to iterate holders inside an instruction, so nothing is ever pushed
out. Instead each deposit raises `acc_per_token`, a running total of lamports earned
per staked token since the pool opened, and every staker subtracts whatever the
counter read when they last settled. That difference is what they are owed — the
standard accumulator, and it costs the same whether ten people stake or ten thousand.
It also fixes the obvious attack on a snapshot: you cannot buy in just before a
payout and sell straight after, because you only accrue while the counter is moving
and only for tokens you had staked at the time.

fields.name: mint
docs: The mint whose stakers are paid. Fixed at creation.

fields.name: total_staked
docs: Tokens currently staked, the denominator for every deposit.

fields.name: acc_per_token
docs: Lamports earned per staked token since inception, scaled by `ACC_SCALE`.

fields.name: owed
docs: Lamports this account holds on stakers' behalf, excluding its own rent. Claims
are checked against this so a claim can never eat the rent and close the pool.

types.name: Stake
docs: One staker's position.

fields.name: amount
docs: Tokens this account has in the vault.

fields.name: reward_debt
docs: `amount * acc_per_token / ACC_SCALE` as of the last settlement. Everything the
counter has climbed since is what this staker has not been credited yet.

fields.name: pending
docs: Settled and waiting to be withdrawn.
